title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
abstract: arXiv:2611.24122v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. This retrospective study evaluated two generalist models, RADAR and Merlin, for differentiating liver tumors using a public single-institution multiphase CT dataset (517 cases: hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, breast and colorectal cancer liver metastases, and hemangioma). The models were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using their existing outputs and with linear probing, in which only a linear classifier was trained on frozen image features (stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated five times). In the zero-shot setting, RADAR achieved an accuracy of 54.4% (95% CI: 49.9, 58.8) and a $\kappa$ of 0.37 for four-class differentiation at the portal venous phase and predicted 31% (129 of 421) of malignant tumors as hemangioma. translated_title: 通用型CT基础模型鉴别肝脏肿瘤的能力如何？
translated_abstract: 本回顾性研究评估了两个通用型模型RADAR和Merlin在鉴别肝脏肿瘤方面的表现，所用数据为公开的单中心多期CT数据集（517例，涵盖肝细胞癌、肝内胆管细胞癌、乳腺癌和结直肠癌肝转移瘤以及血管瘤）。模型分别在零样本设置下（直接利用其现有输出）和线性探测设置下进行评估，后者仅在冻结的图像特征上训练一个线性分类器（采用分层五折交叉验证并重复五次）。在零样本设置下，RADAR在门静脉期进行四类鉴别时准确率为54.4%（95% CI：49.9–58.8），κ为0.37，并将31%（421例中的129例）的恶性肿瘤误判为血管瘤。在四种图像特征的线性探测下……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究首次系统评估了RADAR和Merlin两个通用型CT基础模型区分多种肝脏肿瘤的能力，发现其零样本鉴别性能有限，甚至将31%的恶性肿瘤误判为血管瘤，揭示了通用模型“能检测但难鉴别”的局限。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first systematic evaluation of generalist CT foundation models (RADAR and Merlin) for differentiating liver tumor types, revealing limited zero-shot discrimination with 31% of malignancies misclassified as hemangiomas.
